string-array.name: sim_flood_lessons
string-array.item: Moving higher puts distance between you and rising water. Low areas and riverbanks can flood quickly.
Floodwater can hide washed-out pavement and strong currents. Walking or driving through it can sweep you away.
Leaving by the announced route avoids known hazards. A delay or unverified shortcut may expose you to rising water.
A closed attic can trap you. Calling or signaling helps rescuers find you without entering floodwater.
A drop in water level can hide damaged roads and electrical hazards. Wait for the official return instructions.
Clear water can still be unsafe. Use a safe water supply and follow the authorities’ directions about tap water.

string-array.name: sim_flood_situations
string-array.item: Rain is heavy and water is rising outside. The stairs to a higher floor are clear. What is your first move?
Water covers the road toward higher ground. You cannot see the pavement. Which route do you take?
Authorities order evacuation and announce a route that is clear of floodwater. What do you do?
In another part of town, a household reports that rising water has cut off all safe ground-level exits. They are upstairs. What advice is safest?
The water is going down. Authorities still have not cleared your area for return. What do you do?
Officials say floodwater may have contaminated tap water. You have sealed drinking water. What do you use?

string-array.name: sim_power_lessons
string-array.item: A battery-powered light gives you visibility without an open flame or fuel fumes.
Closed doors keep cold air inside longer. Opening them repeatedly speeds up warming.
Generator exhaust contains carbon monoxide. An open garage or nearby window can still let dangerous fumes build up indoors.
A fallen line can still be live. Keep away and report it from a safe place.
Getting emergency help and following an established backup plan addresses the immediate danger. Waiting delays help.
After four hours without power, a refrigerator without another cold source may no longer keep perishables safe. Smell and taste cannot rule out contamination.
